CSS `dock.css`): areas `start` and `end` (beside the rows, logical sides) and `bottom`. Each area can be resized by
its edge (also with the arrow keys), collapsed to a strip, closed, or moved to another area; two panels in one area
become tabs.

```ts

type Potion = { id: string; name: string; colour: string; doses: number };

const messages: GridMessages = {
  ...EN,
  text: { ...EN.text, ...EN_DOCK.text, ...EN_COLUMNS.text, ...EN_FILTERS.text, ...EN_FILTERS_PANEL.text, ...EN_COLUMN_MENU.text },
};

const chooser = columnsChooser();
const panels = dock({
  open: { columns: 'end' },
  sizes: { min: 200, max: 480 },
  panels: [{
    id: 'notes',
    title: 'Notes',
    area: 'bottom',
    mount(host) {
      const p = host.ownerDocument.createElement('p');
      p.textContent = 'Shake before use.';
      host.append(p);
      return () => p.remove();
    },
  }],
  onChange: (layout) => console.log('dock moved', layout),
});

const grid = createGrid<Potion>(document.getElementById('potions')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 'p1', name: 'Fog in a bottle', colour: 'grey', doses: 3 }],
  columns: [{ id: 'name', header: 'Potion' }, { id: 'colour', header: 'Colour' }, { id: 'doses', header: 'Doses', type: 'number' }],
  getRowId: (p) => p.id,
  messages,
  features: [filters(), chooser, filtersPanel(), columnMenu({ use: { chooser } }), panels],
});

panels.api(grid)?.show('notes');
panels.api(grid)?.move('filters', 'start');
```

- The panels' ids: `columns` (the chooser), `filters` (the filters panel), and the ids of your own panels.
- `open: { id: area }` shows a panel there at the start; otherwise the chooser waits at the end until opened (the
  column menu's « Choose columns », or `chooser.api(grid)?.open()`), and your panels wait at their `area` (`end` by
  default) until `api.show(id)`.
- Your panel's `mount(host)` builds its content and may return a cleanup function.
- `api`: `show`, `hide`, `move`, `collapse`, `resize`, `layout()`, `setLayout(layout)`. With the [state](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgrid/guides/state/)
  feature, where each panel stands is saved with the rest of the grid's state.
- A floating window (area `float`) is planned, not there yet: it is refused with a warning.

Every option of `dock()` will have its place under [Features](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgrid/features/).

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgrid/guides/export-print/ -->

# Export and print

The grid writes what it shows to a file — CSV, Excel or JSON — and prints it as a real table. The demo has the three
files and the print above it, and the same in its right-click menu: sort or filter first, the file follows.

## CSV and Excel

`csvExport({ canExport })` from `@dzgrid/dom/export` writes the grid's rows to a CSV file, and to an Excel file
(`.xlsx`) with `xlsx: true` (texts `-export`). The file holds the visible columns in their order, the sort and the
filters; values are written as values (ISO days, instants in the grid's zone, numbers a spreadsheet can add up), or as
the cells show them with `text: 'display'`.

```ts

type Kettle = { id: string; model: string; litres: number; boughtOn: string };

const exporter = csvExport({
  canExport: true,
  xlsx: true,
  separator: ';',
  fileName: ({ scope }) => `kettles-${scope}`,
});
const messages: GridMessages = { ...EN, text: { ...EN.text, ...EN_EXPORT.text } };

createGrid<Kettle>(document.getElementById('kettles')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 'k1', model: 'Whistling Wren', litres: 1.7, boughtOn: '2024-12-01' }],
  columns: [
    { id: 'model', header: 'Model' },
    { id: 'litres', header: 'Litres', type: 'number' },
    { id: 'boughtOn', header: 'Bought on', type: 'day' },
  ],
  getRowId: (k) => k.id,
  messages,
  selection: { mode: 'multi' },
  features: [exporter],
});

exporter.bind(document.getElementById('csv')!, { scope: 'displayed' });
exporter.bind(document.getElementById('xlsx')!, { scope: 'displayed', format: 'xlsx' });
document.getElementById('selected')!.addEventListener('click', async () => {
  const outcome = await exporter.run('selected');   // 'done' | 'refused' | 'failed' | 'cancelled' | 'busy'
  console.log(outcome);
});
```

- Scopes: `'displayed'` (the rows shown now: the current page when paged), `'selected'`, `'all'` (every row the
  query matches, on every page; the filters still apply).
- `canExport: true`, or a function that may refuse (`{ ok: false, reason }`) — a place for your own permission rule.
- A text starting like a formula (`=`, `+`, `-`, `@`) gets a leading `'` so a spreadsheet does not run it; a number
  such as `-5` never does. `numbers: 'excel'` (the default) writes the locale's decimal mark when the separator is
  `;`, `numbers: 'raw'` the machine form. `csv: 'text'` on a column keeps identifiers such as `0123` as text.
- The file is built in chunks so the page never freezes; `exporter.cancel()` stops it, `onProgress` follows it.
- With server data, the grid holds only some rows: give `exportAll(request, { signal, progress })`, which asks your
  server for the file (the request carries the query in wire form) and returns `{ url }` or `{ blob }`.
- The right-click menu offers the same: `contextMenu({ use: { csv: exporter, xlsx: exporter.xlsx } })`.
- In Angular: `<button [dzgExport]="exporter" dzgExportScope="displayed">` (directive `DzgExport`).

Every option of `csvExport()` will have its place under [Features](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgrid/features/).

## JSON

The same feature writes a JSON file: `run(scope, { format: 'json' })` or `bind(button, { format: 'json' })` — no
option to switch it on, its code is fetched at the first JSON export. The file is one array of objects keyed by the
column ids, in screen order, with raw values: numbers, `true` / `false`, days `'YYYY-MM-DD'`, instants as ISO UTC text
with `Z`, enum codes, `null` for an empty cell (`text: 'display'` writes what the cells show). Group and totals rows
are not written; `canExport` and `exportAll` see `request.format === 'json'`.

```ts

declare const exporter: CsvExport;
exporter.bind(document.getElementById('json')!, { scope: 'all', format: 'json' });
```

## Import a file

`fileImport({ onRows })` from `@dzgrid/dom/import` reads a CSV or Excel (`.xlsx`) file dropped on the grid, or picked
with your own button (`api(grid).bind(button)`, the keyboard path), in the browser. The first non-empty line is the
header, matched to your columns by title or id (case and accents aside); each cell goes through its column's type as
if typed in the grid's language. **The grid never changes its rows**: `onRows(rows, problems, file)` gets one object
per line, at each column's `field` (or id), and you decide — add them, replace, or show a preview. A refused cell is
left out and told as a problem (`import-cell`, path `rows[3].qty`, its code), never with its value. Excel files are
inflated by the browser's `DecompressionStream`; the reading code is fetched at the first file. Texts `-import`.

```ts

type Jar = { id: string; flavour: string; grams: number };
let jars: Jar[] = [{ id: 'j1', flavour: 'Fig', grams: 250 }];
const messages: GridMessages = { ...EN, text: { ...EN.text, ...EN_IMPORT.text } };
const importer = fileImport({
  accept: ['csv', 'xlsx'],
  onRows: (rows, problems) => {
    if (problems.length) console.warn(problems);
    jars = [...jars, ...rows.map((r, i) => ({ ...(r as Omit<Jar, 'id'>), id: `new-${Date.now()}-${i}` }))];
    grid.update({ rows: jars });
  },
});
const grid = createGrid<Jar>(document.getElementById('jars')!, {
  rows: jars,
  columns: [{ id: 'flavour', header: 'Flavour' }, { id: 'grams', header: 'Grams', type: 'number' }],
  getRowId: (j) => j.id,
  messages,
  features: [importer],
});
importer.api(grid)!.bind(document.getElementById('import-button')!);
```

## Print

`print(grid, { title })` from `@dzgrid/dom/print` prints the rows as they are on screen — same columns, order, sort and
filters, not only the rows scrolled into view — as a real table: headers repeated on each page, no row cut in two,
right to left in Arabic, a dark theme printed light (texts `-print`, CSS `print.css`). At most 5 000 rows
(`maxRows`); beyond, a line says how many were printed. A grid with server pages prints the page shown.

```ts

type Bell = { id: string; tower: string; note: string };

const messages: GridMessages = { ...EN, text: { ...EN.text, ...EN_PRINT.text } };
const grid = createGrid<Bell>(document.getElementById('bells')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 'b1', tower: 'Saltmarsh', note: 'F sharp' }],
  columns: [{ id: 'tower', header: 'Tower' }, { id: 'note', header: 'Note' }],
  getRowId: (b) => b.id,
  messages,
});

document.getElementById('print')!.addEventListener('click', () => void print(grid, { title: 'Bells of the coast' }));
printOnMenu(grid, { title: 'Bells of the coast' });   // the browser's own Ctrl+P prints the whole grid too
```

`print(grid, { header: false })` leaves the header rows out (they are printed by default, even on a grid with
`headers: 'hidden'`). `print` is a function, not a feature: nothing is loaded until it is called. `printOnMenu(grid)`
makes the browser's own print command (Ctrl+P, the File menu) print the whole grid as well; without it, that command
prints only what the page shows. In Angular, pass `ctrl.grid()` to both.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgrid/guides/state/ -->

# State

`gridState()` from `@dzgrid/dom/state` reads and restores the grid's state: the columns (order, width, hidden,
pinned), header groups, sort, filters, quick search, page and page size, density, grouped columns, the dock's layout,
the pivot. A state is a plain, versioned object (`{ v: 1, … }`) you can store anywhere. It never holds row data, but
it does hold what the user typed into filters.

```ts

type Lantern = { id: string; street: string; lit: boolean; height: number };

const state = gridState({
  initial: { v: 1, sort: [{ column: 'street', dir: 'asc' }] },
  persist: { key: 'lanterns-grid' },
  debounce: 300,
});

const grid = createGrid<Lantern>(document.getElementById('lanterns')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 'l1', street: 'Wick lane', lit: true, height: 3.5 }],
  columns: [
    { id: 'street', header: 'Street' },
    { id: 'lit', header: 'Lit', type: 'boolean' },
    { id: 'height', header: 'Height (m)', type: 'number' },
  ],
  getRowId: (l) => l.id,
  messages: EN,
  features: [state],
  onEvent: (e) => {
    if (e.type === 'stateChanged') save(e.state);
  },
});

function save(s: GridState) { console.log(JSON.stringify(s)); }

const api = state.api(grid);
const saved = api?.state();
if (saved) api?.setState(saved);   // returns the problems of a state it could not fully read
api?.reset();                      // back to the columns and options the grid was made with
```

- `initial` is applied before the first paint, and on a server before the first request: one request at start.
- `persist: { key, include? }` keeps the state in `localStorage` under that key and restores it at start; blocked or
  full storage throws nothing (one `state-storage` warning). `persistLocal(grid, key)` does the same for a grid made
  without the option.
- `stateChanged` comes after a pause (`debounce`, 300 ms) following a user's change: a resized column, a sort, a
  filter, a panel moved.
- A restore never throws. Unknown or removed column ids are skipped (warning `state-column`), columns the state does
  not name keep their settings and go after the named ones, a field of the wrong type is skipped; a state written by
  a newer version (`v` higher) is refused whole (`state-version`).
- Not saved: open rows, the selection, the focus, the scroll position, edits in progress.

Every option of `gridState()` will have its place under [Features](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgrid/features/).

## In the address

`toSearchParams(state)` and `fromSearchParams(params)` write the state as one compact parameter (`?grid=1.…`) and read
it back. Typed filter values and the search may be names or record numbers, and an address reaches the browser
history, server logs and `Referer` headers: they are left out unless you ask with `include: ['filter', 'quick']`.

```ts

export function writeAddress(state: GridState): void {
  const { params } = toSearchParams(state, { name: 'grid' });
  history.replaceState(null, '', `?${params.toString()}`);
}

export function readAddress(): GridState | null {
  return fromSearchParams(new URLSearchParams(location.search), { name: 'grid' }).state;
}
```

The helpers never touch `history` themselves: you choose `pushState` or `replaceState`. In Angular, `[state]`
restores a state, `(stateChanged)` hears it, and `ctrl.resetState()` resets.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgrid/guides/theming-rtl/ -->

# Theming and right to left

## The theme

`@dzgrid/dom` injects the grid's layout CSS by itself; `@dzgrid/theme` makes it presentable (colours, lines, header,
hover, selection, focus, popups), light and dark, checked for contrast. Each feature with a look has its own sheet,
loaded after `dzgrid.css`: `columns.css`, `menu.css`, `grouping.css`, `pivot.css`, `edit.css`, `range.css`,
`fill.css`, `dock.css`, `columns-panel.css`, `filters-panel.css`, `find.css`, `search.css`, `print.css`,
`row-drag.css`, `pinned-rows.css`, `row-numbers.css`, `fresh-rows.css`; `variables.css` for the presentation knobs
(below).

```ts
```

- **Cascade layer.** Every rule sits in the layer `dzgrid`: your own classes win without `!important`. When you layer
  your own CSS, name the order once, first: `@layer theme, base, dzgrid, components, utilities;`. With an unlayered
  reset (Tailwind 3's preflight, Bootstrap's Reboot), load the `*.unlayered.css` copies instead.
- **Bridges.** `tailwind.css` (Tailwind 4), `tailwind3.css`, `bootstrap.css` (5.3, follows `data-bs-theme`) map the
  grid's colours, font and corners to your framework's.
- **Showcase themes.** `midnight.css` and `clinic.css`, each with a light and a dark twin; `data-dzg-skin="midnight"`
  on a container styles only that area.

## Colours and sizes

Colours are CSS variables only. The palette (shared with tzslot), each a `light-dark()` pair on `:root`: `--tz-bg`,
`--tz-bg-raised`, `--tz-fg`, `--tz-fg-muted`, `--tz-border`, `--tz-accent`, `--tz-accent-fg`, `--tz-danger`,
`--tz-warning`, `--tz-success`. What the grid derives, set on any ancestor of `.dzg`: `--dzg-font`, `--dzg-radius`,
`--dzg-cell-padding-inline`, `--dzg-header-bg`, `--dzg-row-hover-bg`, `--dzg-row-selected-bg`, `--dzg-focus-ring`,
`--dzg-line`, `--dzg-pill-radius`, `--dzg-header-size`, `--dzg-select-bar`, `--dzg-flash`, `--dzg-flash-color` —
every one in the table below. This site's own accent is the grid's `--tz-accent`: switch the site to dark and every
demo follows.

```css
:root { --tz-accent: light-dark(#7c3aed, #c4b5fd); }
.dzg { --dzg-radius: 6px; --dzg-font: "Atkinson Hyperlegible", system-ui, sans-serif; }
.dzg-cell.is-late { color: var(--tz-danger); }
```

### Every variable

Set any of them on an ancestor of `.dzg` (or on `.dzg`), or from code with the `theme` setting below. *Sheet* says
which stylesheet reads it: **base** = `dzgrid.css` (and the layout `@dzgrid/dom` injects); **variables** =
`@dzgrid/theme/variables.css`, loaded after `dzgrid.css` (`variables.unlayered.css` after the unlayered copy) — it
changes nothing by itself; a feature's sheet is named. *Key* is the `theme` setting's key.

| Variable | Key | What it sets | Default | Sheet |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--tz-bg`, `--tz-bg-raised`, `--tz-fg`, `--tz-fg-muted`, `--tz-border` | `bg`, `bgRaised`, `fg`, `fgMuted`, `border` | The palette's surfaces, text and lines | tzslot's palette | base |
| `--tz-accent`, `--tz-accent-fg`, `--tz-danger`, `--tz-warning`, `--tz-success` | `accent`, `accentFg`, `danger`, `warning`, `success` | Accent and tones | tzslot's palette | base |
| `--dzg-font` | `font` | The grid's `font` shorthand | inherited | base |
| `--dzg-radius` | `radius` | Corners of buttons, popups, tooltips (and the frame) | `.375rem` | base |
| `--dzg-line` | `line` | Width of every line | `1px` | base |
| `--dzg-pill-radius` | `pillRadius` | A badge's corners | `1em` | base |
| `--dzg-cell-padding-inline` | `cellPaddingInline` | Cells' side padding (× the density) | `.5rem` | base |
| `--dzg-cell-padding-block` | `cellPaddingBlock` | A wrapped cell's top and bottom padding | `0` | variables |
| `--dzg-cell-align-block` | `cellAlignBlock` | A wrapped or part-drawn cell's content: `start`, `center`, `end` | top | variables |
| `--dzg-cell-font-size` | `cellFontSize` | The cells' text size | the grid's | variables |
| `--dzg-num-figures` | `numFigures` | Number cells' digits (`normal` to turn equal widths off) | `tabular-nums` | base |
| `--dzg-space` | `space` | The spacing unit: header gap ×1, overlay ×2, popup padding ×3, footer ×1 / ×2 | `.25rem` | variables |
| `--dzg-target-min` | `targetMin` | The smallest button, grip and toggle (WCAG 2.5.8) | `24px` | base |
| `--dzg-header-bg` | `headerBg` | Header, footer, group rows, buttons | `--tz-bg-raised` | base |
| `--dzg-header-fg` | `headerFg` | Header text | `--tz-fg` | variables |
| `--dzg-header-size` | `headerSize` | Header text size | `1em` | base |
| `--dzg-header-weight` | `headerWeight` | Header weight | `600` | variables |
| `--dzg-header-font-family` | `headerFontFamily` | Header font family | the grid's | variables |
| `--dzg-header-tracking` | `headerTracking` | Header letter spacing (never in Arabic) | `normal` | base |
| `--dzg-header-case` | `headerCase` | `uppercase` titles (Arabic has no case) | `none` | variables |
| `--dzg-header-align-block` | `headerAlignBlock` | A tall header's title: `start`, `center`, `end` | `center` | variables |
| `--dzg-header-hover-bg` | `headerHoverBg` | A sortable header under the pointer | unchanged | variables |
| `--dzg-frame` | `frame` | The grid's outer edge (a border; `none`) | `--dzg-line` solid `--tz-border` | variables |
| `--dzg-frame-radius` | `frameRadius` | The frame's corners | `--dzg-radius` | variables |
| `--dzg-row-line` | `rowLine` | The line between rows (a border; `none`) | as the frame | variables |
| `--dzg-column-line` | `columnLine` | A line between columns (a border) | `none` | variables |
| `--dzg-header-line` | `headerLine` | The line under each header row | as the frame | variables |
| `--dzg-header-separator`, `-size`, `-height` | `headerSeparator`, `headerSeparatorSize`, `headerSeparatorHeight` | The marks between resizable header cells | `--tz-border`, `2px`, `50%` | variables |
| `--dzg-pinned-column-line` | `pinnedColumnLine` | The pinned columns' edge | as the frame | variables |
| `--dzg-pinned-shadow` | `pinnedShadow` | A `box-shadow` at that edge while content is under it, written for the start side (mirrored by the grid) | none | base |
| `--dzg-detail-line` | `detailLine` | A detail panel's start rule | `3px solid --tz-border` | variables |
| `--dzg-row-odd-bg` | `rowOddBg` | Alternate rows (the 2nd, 4th… shown) | none | base |
| `--dzg-row-hover-bg`, `--dzg-row-selected-bg`, `--dzg-row-active-bg` | `rowHoverBg`, `rowSelectedBg`, `rowActiveBg` | Row under the pointer, selected, holding the focus | tints of the palette | base |
| `--dzg-cell-active-bg`, `--dzg-focus-ring` | `cellActiveBg`, `focusRing` | The focused cell's tint and ring | accent tints | base |
| `--dzg-focus-width` | `focusWidth` | The ring's width (never under 2 px) | `2px` | variables |
| `--dzg-select-bar` | `selectBar` | A selected row's bar at its start | `0` | base |
| `--dzg-stale-fg`, `--dzg-context-fg`, `--dzg-toggle-fg` | `staleFg`, `contextFg`, `toggleFg` | Rows kept while loading, a tree's context rows, chevrons | `--tz-fg-muted` | base |
| `--dzg-detail-bg` | `detailBg` | A detail panel's surface | `--tz-bg-raised` | base |
| `--dzg-group-row-bg` | `groupRowBg` | Group rows and their footers | `--dzg-header-bg` | `grouping.css` |
| `--dzg-pinned-bg`, `--dzg-pinned-line` | `pinnedBg`, `pinnedLine` | Pinned rows' surface and edge | `--tz-bg-raised`, `--tz-fg-muted` | `pinned-rows.css` |
| `--dzg-busy-bar` | `busyBar` | The busy bar | `--tz-accent` | base |
| `--dzg-flash-color` | `flashColor` | A changed value's flash | `--tz-warning` | base |
| `--dzg-fresh-color`, `--dzg-fresh-bg`, `--dzg-fresh-bar` | `freshColor`, `freshBg`, `freshBar` | Rows a refresh brought | `--tz-success`, 14 %, `3px` | `fresh-rows.css` |
| `--dzg-saving-color`, `--dzg-saved-color`, `--dzg-refused-color`, `--dzg-refused-bg` | `savingColor`, `savedColor`, `refusedColor`, `refusedBg` | Save marks, a refused value | tones | `edit.css`, base |
| `--dzg-editor-border` | `editorBorder` | An open editor's frame | `--dzg-focus-ring` | `edit.css` |
| `--dzg-range-bg`, `--dzg-range-edge`, `--dzg-fill-handle` | `rangeBg`, `rangeEdge`, `fillHandle` | A block of cells, its edge, the fill handle | selection tint, `--tz-success` | `range.css`, `fill.css` |
| `--dzg-move-bar`, `--dzg-resize-mode` | `moveBar`, `resizeMode` | Where a moved column lands; the keyboard resize | `--tz-accent` | `columns.css` |
| `--dzg-search-mark`, `--dzg-find-color`, `--dzg-find-bg`, `--dzg-find-current-bg`, `--dzg-find-mark`, `--dzg-find-mark-current` | `searchMark`, `findColor`, `findBg`, `findCurrentBg`, `findMark`, `findMarkCurrent` | Search and find marks | palette mixes | `search.css`, `find.css` |
| `--dzg-box-size`, `--dzg-box-radius` | `boxSize`, `boxRadius` | The selection box (its column keeps its width) | `1rem`, `.25rem` | variables |
| `--dzg-box-on-bg`, `--dzg-box-edge` | `boxOnBg`, `boxEdge` | A ticked box's fill, an unticked one's edge | `--tz-accent`, `--tz-fg-muted` | variables |
| `--dzg-icon-size` | `iconSize` | Sort mark, chevrons, grip, funnel, the app's icons in buttons | each mark's own (funnel `12px`) | variables, feature layouts |
| `--dzg-popup-bg`, `--dzg-popup-shadow` | `popupBg`, `popupShadow` | Filter popups and menus | `--tz-bg`, a soft shadow | variables |
| `--dzg-tooltip-bg`, `--dzg-tooltip-fg` | `tooltipBg`, `tooltipFg` | The tooltip | `--tz-fg` on `--tz-bg` reversed | variables |
| `--dzg-input-bg`, `--dzg-input-border` | `inputBg`, `inputBorder` | The filters' boxes | `--tz-bg`, `--tz-fg-muted` | variables |
| `--dzg-button-bg`, `--dzg-button-border` | `buttonBg`, `buttonBorder` | Pager, filter footer, retry buttons (Apply keeps the accent) | `--dzg-header-bg`, `--tz-fg-muted` | variables |
| `--dzg-menu-item-height`, `--dzg-menu-disabled` | `menuItemHeight`, `menuDisabled` | Menu items (never under 24 px), a disabled one | `32px`, `--tz-fg-muted` | `menu.css`, `columns.css` |
| `--dzg-panel-bg` | `panelBg` | The dock and the filters panel | `--tz-bg` | `dock.css`, `filters-panel.css` |
| `--dzg-chip-bg`, `--dzg-chip-hover-bg`, `--dzg-control-active-bg` | `chipBg`, `chipHoverBg`, `controlActiveBg` | Chips; a pressed panel button | accent / text mixes | feature sheets |
| `--dzg-scrollbar`, `--dzg-scrollbar-thumb`, `--dzg-scrollbar-thumb-active` | `scrollbar`, `scrollbarThumb`, `scrollbarThumbActive` | Thin or system scrollbars, the thumb at rest and under the pointer | `thin`, `--tz-border`, `--tz-fg-muted` | `dzgrid.comfort.css` |

Read-only (written by the grid; no key): `--dzg-row-height`, `--dzg-header-height`, `--dzg-density` (`.75` compact,
`1`, `1.25` spacious: the side padding follows the density; `.dzg { --dzg-density: 1 }` in your own CSS keeps it fixed).
Pinned columns' own surface: `.dzg-seg-start`, `.dzg-seg-end` in your CSS (they follow hover and selection).

### The `theme` setting

The demo below sets a few of these keys from code on one grid only: alternate rows, lines between columns, a lighter
header weight.

```ts

type Hive = { id: string; name: string; frames: number };

const grid = createGrid<Hive>(document.getElementById('hives')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 'h1', name: 'Orchard hive', frames: 10 }],
  columns: [{ id: 'name', header: 'Hive' }, { id: 'frames', header: 'Frames', type: 'number' }],
  getRowId: (h) => h.id,
  messages: EN,
  theme: { accent: 'light-dark(#0f766e, #5eead4)', rowOddBg: 'color-mix(in srgb, var(--tz-accent) 6%, var(--tz-bg))', headerWeight: 500, columnLine: 'var(--dzg-line) solid var(--tz-border)' },
  features: [theming()],
});
grid.update({ theme: { headerWeight: 700 } });   // live: the previous keys not given again are taken away
```

The keys are the table's; each is written on the grid's root, so it wins over your stylesheets for that grid only. A
value is a CSS value or a number (`600`); a key not in the table or a value with `;`, `{`, `}`, `<`, `\`, `!` or
`url(` is told (`invalid-setting`, path `settings.theme.<key>`) and left out. Contrast is yours to keep:
`npm run check:contrast -- --palette` checks a palette file.

### Icons

The grid draws its own marks (characters and shapes, no file, in the text colour). To draw yours:

```ts

type Hive = { id: string; name: string; frames: number };
const funnel = document.querySelector<SVGSVGElement>('#my-funnel')!;   // an <svg> already in the page: copied

createGrid<Hive>(document.getElementById('hives')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 'h1', name: 'Orchard hive', frames: 10 }],
  columns: [{ id: 'name', header: 'Hive' }, { id: 'frames', header: 'Frames', type: 'number' }],
  getRowId: (h) => h.id,
  messages: EN,
  icons: { sortAsc: '<svg viewBox="0 0 16 16"><path d="M8 3l5 8H3z"/></svg>', filter: funnel },
  features: [theming()],
});
```

Names: `sortAsc`, `sortDesc`, `filter`, `filterActive` (a filtered column's; else `filter` in the accent — give it to
keep a mark that is not colour alone), `menu`, `chevron` (trees, details, header groups: turned and mirrored as the
default), `submenu`, `grip`. An SVG string or element (copied). Its shape is drawn in the mark's colour and size
(`--dzg-icon-size`), whatever its own fill. Refused, the default kept and `invalid-setting` told: anything but `<svg>`
with shapes, groups, gradients, `use` and `title`; a `<script>`, `<style>` or `<foreignObject>`; an `on…` attribute; a
link or `url()` outside the icon (only `#…`); more than 20 000 characters. Drawn as a `data:` image: a CSP must allow
`img-src data:`. With `injectStyles: false`, load `ICONS_CSS` from `@dzgrid/dom/theme` too.

### Alternate rows, lines, the pinned edge

```css
.dzg {
  --dzg-row-odd-bg: color-mix(in srgb, var(--tz-accent) 6%, var(--tz-bg));     /* base */
  --dzg-pinned-shadow: 6px 0 6px -4px color-mix(in srgb, var(--tz-fg) 35%, transparent); /* base */
  --dzg-column-line: var(--dzg-line) solid var(--tz-border);                     /* variables.css */
  --dzg-frame: none;                                                             /* variables.css */
}
```

A header title follows its column's `align` (numbers at the end); `headerAlign` on a column places it otherwise.

**Light and dark** follow the system; `data-theme="light"` or `data-theme="dark"` on any ancestor forces one.

**Row height** comes from the `density` setting (`compact` 28 px, `comfortable` 32 px, the default, `spacious` 40 px)
or `rowHeight` in pixels, which wins. Rows follow the reader's text zoom. The column menu can offer the density to the
user (`columnMenu({ density: true })`), and the [state](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgrid/guides/state/) keeps it.

**Header height**: the header rows are one row high unless `headerHeight` (pixels, 24 at least, live) makes them
taller — `{ rowHeight: 40, headerHeight: 70 }`, Angular `[headerHeight]="70"`, `<dz-grid header-height="70">`. It
sets the column headers' row and the column-group rows above it (a 70 px header with one group row is 140 px); the
filter row keeps the row height. It follows the text zoom as rows do; vertical titles still grow the row when they
need more. The grid writes it on its root as `--dzg-header-height` (read-only, as `--dzg-row-height`).

Since 1.10.0 the group rows have their own height: `headerHeight: { columns: 70, groups: 30 }` (`columns` absent: the
row height; `groups` absent: the columns'). The filter row has its own too: `filters({ floating: true, rowHeight: 44 })`.
Titles on several lines (`headerWrap`, [columns](https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgrid/guides/columns/)) grow the column headers' row; the taller wins.

**The grid's height comes from its container**, never from its rows: give the host a height (fixed, a flex or grid
share, `100dvh` minus a bar) and the grid fills it whatever its row count (since 1.11.0); the rows scroll inside. There is no « as tall as its rows » mode — the page would
jump each time a filter changes the count.

**Column under the pointer** (1.10.0): `columnHover()` from `@dzgrid/dom/column-hover` writes `data-hover-col` on the
root and `data-col-hover` on that column's cells (mouse and pen only, never the keyboard); the tint is yours:

```css
.dzg { --dzg-column-hover-bg: color-mix(in srgb, var(--tz-accent) 8%, transparent); }
```

## Right to left

Direction is designed in: pinned columns, scrolling, the arrow keys (in Arabic, → moves toward the start, which is on
the right), popups, the tree's indent and the theme all follow it. Everything in DzGrid speaks of **start** and
**end**, never left and right: `pinned: 'start'`, `align: 'end'`, the dock's `start` area.

```ts

type Souk = { id: string; name: string; stalls: number };

const grid = createGrid<Souk>(document.getElementById('souks')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 's1', name: 'سوق النجوم', stalls: 48 }],
  columns: [
    { id: 'name', header: 'السوق', pinned: 'start' },
    { id: 'stalls', header: 'الدكاكين', type: 'number', align: 'end' },
  ],
  getRowId: (s) => s.id,
  messages: AR,
  locale: 'ar-DZ',
  direction: 'rtl',
  numerals: 'locale',
});

grid.update({ direction: 'auto' });   // follow the nearest `dir` attribute instead
```

- `direction`: `'ltr'`, `'rtl'`, or `'auto'` (the nearest ancestor's `dir`).
- `numerals: 'locale'` shows the language's own digits (Arabic-Indic for `ar`); the default `'latn'` keeps 0–9.
- Sorting and searching follow the language: hamza forms, short vowels and tatweel, Arabic-Indic digits.
- Your own CSS should use logical properties as well: `margin-inline-start`, `inset-inline-end`, `text-align: start`.
- Three languages ship: `EN`, `FR`, `AR` (`@dzgrid/dom/locales/*`), each feature with its own bundle, plural rules
  included. Another language is a `GridMessages` object of your own with the same keys; `checkMessages(messages)`
  throws, naming the keys that are missing.

---

<!-- https://plinthworks.github.io/dzgrid/guides/accessibility/ -->

# Accessibility

DzGrid follows the WAI-ARIA grid pattern (a treegrid for trees and groups) and aims at WCAG 2.2 AA. The draft
conformance report is
[`docs/a11y/acr-wcag22.md`](https://github.com/plinthworks/dzgrid/blob/main/docs/a11y/acr-wcag22.md): it says,
criterion by criterion, what is checked and how. Its screen-reader listening is not done yet, so the criteria that
rest on what a screen reader says are marked « partially supports » until then.

## What the grid does

- **One tab stop.** Tab enters the grid at the focused cell; the arrows, Page Up / Down, Home / End and Ctrl+Home /
  End move inside; Tab leaves. The focus is never lost when rows are sorted, filtered, reloaded or scrolled away
  (rows are virtualised: the focused row is kept).
- **Roles and states.** `role="grid"` (or `treegrid`), real row and column counts (`aria-rowcount`, `aria-colcount`)
  even when only some rows are drawn, `aria-sort` on sorted headers, `aria-selected` and `aria-expanded` on rows,
  `aria-readonly` where editing is on.
- **Announcements.** Sorting, filtering, a page change, an export, a refused edit, a row moved are said through a live
  region, in the grid's language, with plurals.
- **Every action has a keyboard way**: column moves and sizes, row moves (Alt+Shift+arrows), the fill (Ctrl+D /
  Ctrl+R), the dock's edges and tabs, the menus (Shift+F10 or the Menu key). Dragging is never the only way.
- **Targets** of 24 px at least; **contrast** of 4.5:1 for every text and 3:1 for every part, checked by script on
  every colour pair, light and dark; **forced colours** (Windows High Contrast) use the system's colours; motion
  follows `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Zoom and text size.** Page zoom to 400 % works; at 320 CSS pixels wide nothing scrolls sideways outside the
  grid; rows grow with the reader's default text size.

Try it on the grid below with the keyboard only: Tab into it, move with the arrows, Enter on a title sorts, Shift+F10
opens a title's menu, Space selects a row.

## What is left to you

- **A name.** Give the `label` setting (`label="Invoices"`, `[label]` in Angular), or every grid on the page has the
  same generic name (« Data grid »).
- **Translated texts.** Headers are your strings, already in the user's language; the grid's own sentences come from
  `messages` (English, French and Arabic ship). A part's own texts go through its context's `msg('app.key')`.
- **The page's language and direction** (`lang` and `dir` on `<html>`): the grid follows `direction: 'auto'` and
  says its sentences in its `messages`' language.
- **Custom parts keep their promises.** A cell part draws inside a cell the grid owns (role, focus, keys stay the
  grid's); a button in it must be a real `<button type="button">` with a name. Do not move the focus yourself from a
  part; say things with the context's `announce(text)`.
- **Colours** only through the theme's variables (`--tz-*`, `--dzg-*`), so the contrast checks and the dark and
  forced-colours modes keep working. Do not convey meaning by colour alone: a `badge` part writes its text too.
- **Problems.** A `Problem` never carries row data (rows may be personal), only a code, a path and a short detail:
  log them, do not show them to the user as they are.

```ts

type Lighthouse = { id: string; name: string; range: number };

document.documentElement.lang = 'en';
document.documentElement.dir = 'ltr';

const grid = createGrid<Lighthouse>(document.getElementById('lighthouses')!, {
  rows: [{ id: 'p1', name: 'Mistcape Light', range: 22 }],
  columns: [{ id: 'name', header: 'Lighthouse' }, { id: 'range', header: 'Range (nmi)', type: 'number' }],
  getRowId: (p) => p.id,
  messages: EN,
  locale: 'en-GB',
  label: 'Lighthouses of the coast',
  direction: 'auto',
});

grid.api.announce('List updated');
```

The owner's hand-made listening route (keyboard and screen readers, the essential path) is
[`docs/a11y/parcours-essentiel.md`](https://github.com/plinthworks/dzgrid/blob/main/docs/a11y/parcours-essentiel.md).
